mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines lattice energy in an ionic solid?

options.A: Energy required to break one mole of ionic solid into gaseous ions.
options.B: Energy released when one mole of gaseous ions combine to form one mole of solid lattice.
options.C: Energy needed to ionize a gaseous atom.
options.D: Energy released during electron affinity of a non‑metal atom.

mcqs.answer: Energy released when one mole of gaseous ions combine to form one mole of solid lattice.
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy is the enthalpy change when gaseous cations and anions combine to form one mole of an ionic solid. It is distinct from ionization energy (option C) and electron affinity (option D), and it is the opposite of the energy required to separate the lattice (option A).

mcqs.learning_point: Relate ionic size to lattice properties
mcqs.question: Given two ionic compounds, NaCl (Na⁺ radius ≈ 102 pm, Cl⁻ ≈ 181 pm) and CsI (Cs⁺ ≈ 167 pm, I⁻ ≈ 220 pm), which will have the higher lattice energy?

options.A: NaCl, because the smaller ions produce a stronger electrostatic attraction.
options.B: CsI, because larger ions are more polarizable and increase lattice energy.
options.C: Both have the same lattice energy because they have the same charge magnitude.
options.D: Lattice energy depends only on the charges, not on ionic sizes.

mcqs.answer: NaCl, because the smaller ions produce a stronger electrostatic attraction.
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy increases when the distance between ions decreases. Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are smaller than Cs⁺ and I⁻, so the inter‑ionic distance in NaCl is shorter, giving a larger (more exothermic) lattice energy. Options B, C, and D ignore the size factor.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes a typical property of ionic compounds?

options.A: They are good conductors of electricity in the solid state.
options.C: They are soluble in non‑polar solvents such as hexane.
options.D: They are brittle and possess high melting points.

mcqs.answer: They are brittle and possess high melting points.
mcqs.explanation: Ionic solids consist of a rigid lattice of oppositely charged ions, making them brittle and giving them high melting and boiling points. They conduct electricity only when molten or dissolved (not in solid form), contrary to option A. Options B and C are incorrect because ionic compounds generally have high melting points and are soluble in polar solvents like water, not non‑polar ones.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain formation of cations and anions
mcqs.question: When magnesium metal reacts with chlorine gas according to the equation Mg + Cl₂ → MgCl₂, which description correctly represents the formation of ions?

options.A: Mg loses two electrons to form Mg²⁺, and each Cl atom gains one electron to form Cl⁻.
options.B: Mg gains two electrons to become Mg²⁻, while each Cl atom loses one electron.
options.C: Both Mg and Cl share electrons equally, forming a covalent bond.
options.D: Mg loses one electron and each Cl atom gains two electrons.

mcqs.answer: Mg loses two electrons to form Mg²⁺, and each Cl atom gains one electron to form Cl⁻.
mcqs.explanation: In ionic bonding, the metal (Mg) loses electrons to achieve a stable octet, forming a cation (Mg²⁺). Each chlorine atom gains one electron, becoming an anion (Cl⁻). The resulting electrostatic attraction between Mg²⁺ and two Cl⁻ ions yields MgCl₂. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect electron transfer processes.

mcqs.question: A common misconception is that in an ionic bond the electrons are shared equally between the atoms. Which statement correctly describes the actual process?

options.A: Electrons are transferred from the metal to the non‑metal, creating oppositely charged ions that attract each other.
options.B: Electrons are equally shared, forming a covalent bond.
options.C: Electrons are transferred from the non‑metal to the metal.
options.D: No electron movement occurs; only nuclear forces hold the atoms together.

mcqs.answer: Electrons are transferred from the metal to the non‑metal, creating oppositely charged ions that attract each other.
mcqs.explanation: Ionic bonding involves complete transfer of valence electrons from a low‑electronegativity metal to a high‑electronegativity non‑metal, producing cations and anions that are held together by electrostatic forces. Options B, C, and D describe either covalent bonding, the opposite transfer direction, or a physically impossible scenario.

mcqs.question: Why is lattice energy considered a measure of the strength of the ionic bond in a crystal?

options.A: Because it equals the energy required to ionize the constituent atoms.
options.B: Because it represents the energy released when gaseous ions combine to form the solid lattice, reflecting the electrostatic attraction.
options.C: Because it is identical to the enthalpy of formation of the compound.
options.D: Because it measures the kinetic energy of ions moving within the lattice.

mcqs.answer: Because it represents the energy released when gaseous ions combine to form the solid lattice, reflecting the electrostatic attraction.
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy quantifies the exothermic process of bringing oppositely charged ions from infinite separation to their positions in the crystal lattice. A larger (more negative) lattice energy indicates stronger ionic bonding. Options A and C confuse lattice energy with ionization energy and enthalpy of formation, while D misinterprets it as kinetic energy.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate ionic size to lattice properties
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the effect of ionic size on lattice energy?

options.A: Larger cation and larger anion always give a higher lattice energy than smaller ions.
options.B: A smaller cation paired with a smaller anion results in a higher lattice energy than larger ions.
options.C: Ionic size does not affect lattice energy; only the magnitude of the charges matters.
options.D: Lattice energy is highest when one ion is very large and the other is very small.

mcqs.answer: A smaller cation paired with a smaller anion results in a higher lattice energy than larger ions.
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy is inversely proportional to the distance between ion centers. Smaller ions bring charges closer together, increasing electrostatic attraction and thus lattice energy. Option A is opposite to the trend, C ignores size, and D describes an unrealistic extreme that would actually reduce lattice energy due to poor packing.

mcqs.question: All of the following are typical characteristics of ionic compounds except:

options.B: Good electrical conductivity when molten or dissolved in water.
options.C: Solubility in water but insolubility in non‑polar organic solvents.
options.D: High electrical conductivity in the solid state.

mcqs.answer: High electrical conductivity in the solid state.
mcqs.explanation: Ionic solids consist of fixed ions; they do not conduct electricity until the lattice is broken (by melting or dissolution). Hence option D is false. Options A, B, and C correctly describe ionic compounds.
